items.name: Global illumination by path tracing
acceptance: An enclosed box converges without an added ambient term.

items.name: Multiple importance sampling for lights and surfaces
acceptance: Small emitters and rough reflections converge to the same reference mean.

items.name: Adaptive sampling
acceptance: Stopping statistics remain defined for dark pixels and bright edges.

items.name: Progressive accumulation
items.benefit: Refine a visible result over time
acceptance: A scene edit invalidates the correct buffers without mixing revisions.

items.name: Spatial antialiasing and pixel filtering
items.benefit: Resolve fine silhouettes and texture detail
acceptance: Thin wires retain coverage without unstable stair steps.

items.name: Russian roulette and explicit bounce limits
acceptance: Compensated roulette is distinguished from finite-depth truncation.

items.name: Heterogeneous participating media
acceptance: A bounded test volume has reproducible transmittance and convergence.

items.name: Specialized sampling of difficult paths
items.benefit: Handle rare but important optical paths
acceptance: A difficult-path benchmark reports error and time against a reference.

items.name: Area lights with several shapes
items.benefit: Control source extent and highlight shape
acceptance: Emitter size changes penumbra while the chosen energy policy is preserved.

items.name: Point and spot lights with physical falloff
acceptance: An unobstructed receiver follows the declared distance law.

items.name: Sun with finite angular extent
acceptance: Shadow spread follows distance and angular size.

items.name: IES and LDT photometric distributions
acceptance: Axes, units and total output survive import or documented conversion.

items.name: Sampled emissive meshes
items.benefit: Let visible emitters illuminate the scene
acceptance: A visible panel and its sampling representation contribute energy once.

items.name: Light tree acceleration
acceptance: Many-light output matches a smaller reference within sampling error.

items.name: Light groups and linear gain adjustments
items.benefit: Rebalance contributions in a fixed scene
acceptance: Linear gains reconstruct the reference; RGB recoloring is labelled editorial.

items.name: Light and shadow linking
acceptance: Saved exceptions are visible and never silently replace physical transport.

items.name: OpenPBR-referenced layered appearance
acceptance: Layer combinations respect the declared energy model.

items.name: Dielectric and conductor Fresnel
acceptance: Normal and grazing reference cases agree with analytic expectations.

items.name: Microfacet roughness and energy compensation
acceptance: Increasing roughness does not introduce unexplained energy loss.

items.name: Orientable anisotropy
acceptance: Rotated instances retain their intended material-local direction.

items.name: Independent transparent coating
acceptance: Coat and substrate remain independently editable.

items.name: Surface fibers and textile sheen
acceptance: Grazing highlights change consistently with the fiber model.

items.name: Flakes and effect pigments
acceptance: Sparkle remains stable across distance and resolution.

items.name: Measured BSDF and specialized surface models
acceptance: Units, angular conventions and provenance survive import.

items.name: Smooth and rough refraction
acceptance: A slab and a curved lens agree with geometry and interface orientation.

items.name: Distance-dependent absorption
acceptance: A thickness wedge follows the declared attenuation law.

items.name: Nested dielectrics and media
acceptance: A liquid-filled vial handles air, glass and contents without a false air gap.

items.name: Subsurface scattering
acceptance: Thin and thick regions vary consistently under a fixed light.

items.name: Reflective and refractive caustics
acceptance: A documented caustic target converges without arbitrary brightness boosts.

items.name: Spectral chromatic dispersion
acceptance: A prism reference has the correct ordering and declared spectral assumptions.

items.name: Thin-film interference
acceptance: Angular and thickness variation follow the chosen model.

items.name: Polarization and specialized optical transport
acceptance: Only validated optical configurations advertise this capability.

items.name: Physical texture scale
items.benefit: Keep surface features at real dimensions
acceptance: The same finish retains detail size on different bodies.

items.name: Planar cylindrical and triplanar mapping
items.benefit: Place patterns without fragile UV assumptions
acceptance: Seams and rotated instances are checked at multiple scales.

items.name: Normal and bump detail
acceptance: Data textures avoid color transforms and preserve orientation.

items.name: Adaptive geometric displacement
acceptance: Displaced boundaries retain continuity within a documented tolerance.

items.name: Render-only edge microbevel
items.benefit: Improve edge response without CAD edits
acceptance: The design B-rep and dimensions remain unchanged.

items.name: Decals labels and masks
items.benefit: Apply product markings and layered selections
acceptance: Labels remain sharp, correctly oriented and reversible.

items.name: Localized wear and contamination
acceptance: Wear reveals the intended substrate and avoids unrelated body regions.

items.name: Texture filtering and continuity
acceptance: Distant texture detail remains temporally stable.

items.name: Importance-sampled HDR environments
acceptance: A rotated environment moves illumination and reflections coherently.

items.name: Procedural sky and sun
acceptance: The sun has exactly one owned contribution.

items.name: Ground shadows and reflections
items.benefit: Anchor a product in its scene
acceptance: Support, reflected contact and shadow agree geometrically.

items.name: Three-dimensional environments with parallax
acceptance: Camera translation produces correct foreground displacement.

items.name: Background with explicit lighting links
acceptance: An artistic decoupling is recorded in the saved shot.

items.name: Fog and aerial perspective
acceptance: Physical lunar scenes reject this atmospheric component.

items.name: Volumetric light shafts
acceptance: A beam requires a declared participating medium.

items.name: Coordinated weather and surface state
acceptance: Changing weather exposes which appearance layers it changes.

items.name: Perspective and orthographic cameras
acceptance: Saved framing reopens identically within numeric tolerance.

items.name: Physical depth of field
acceptance: In-focus and out-of-focus reference planes behave consistently.

items.name: Aperture shape and bokeh
acceptance: Out-of-focus highlights retain the declared aperture behavior.

items.name: Lens shift and vertical correction
acceptance: Vertical correction does not silently change model coordinates.

items.name: Motion blur
acceptance: Blur follows the evaluated trajectory throughout the shutter.

items.name: Panoramic and stereo output
acceptance: Projection seams and eye transforms pass a reference scene.

items.name: Photographic backplate calibration
acceptance: Reprojection error and remaining ambiguity are reported.

items.name: Turntables and saved camera poses
acceptance: The orbit targets the selected subject without altering it.

items.name: Declared scene-linear color pipeline
acceptance: Color textures and numeric maps follow different decode paths.

items.name: Display transform
items.benefit: Map the rendered signal to a display
acceptance: Preview and export use the same declared transform.

items.name: Exposure in EV
acceptance: One EV multiplies the linear signal by two before display mapping.

items.name: White balance
acceptance: Neutral reference patches respond consistently to a saved balance.

items.name: Histogram and clipping indicators
items.benefit: Expose lost highlight or shadow information
acceptance: Indicators clearly distinguish scene-linear and display-referred values.

items.name: Contrast curves and saturation
acceptance: Reset restores the underlying rendered signal.

items.name: LUTs and image looks
acceptance: The required input and output spaces travel with the look.

items.name: Proofing and gamut checks
acceptance: Out-of-gamut warnings use a declared transform.

items.name: Denoising with auxiliary buffers
acceptance: Fine wires and labels survive comparison against an unfiltered reference.

items.name: Highlight bloom
acceptance: Bloom does not change the energy used to illuminate geometry.

items.name: Lens flare and aperture diffraction
acceptance: The effect is reproducible and separately disabled.

items.name: Vignette and lens distortion
acceptance: Geometric and brightness changes are recorded as image treatment.

items.name: Chromatic aberration
acceptance: The effect remains distinct from material dispersion.

items.name: Output grain and sharpening
acceptance: The untouched master remains available.

items.name: Object masks and compositing
acceptance: Transparent edges have a documented mask interpretation.

items.name: Inspection occlusion and outlines
acceptance: The physical render avoids double-darkening its global illumination.

items.name: High-quality PNG and TIFF output
acceptance: Decoded output agrees with the displayed image and alpha convention.

items.name: Scene-linear multilayer EXR
acceptance: The file reopens with correct linear values and channel names.

items.name: Transport and diagnostic passes
acceptance: Summed physical contributions reconstruct the intended beauty result.

items.name: Cryptomatte or interoperable equivalent
acceptance: Independent compatible readers recover the declared selections.

items.name: Product-variant render queue
acceptance: Jobs capture immutable requests and never overwrite another result silently.

items.name: Animation image sequences
acceptance: Each frame is labelled by scene time and retains shared settings.

items.name: Render regions and A/B comparison
acceptance: A crop matches the equivalent full-frame region.

items.name: Job continuation and recovery
acceptance: A resumed job validates scene and resource hashes before continuing.

items.name: Executor capability contracts
acceptance: Preflight and start evaluate the same immutable request.

items.name: Intersection acceleration and instances
acceptance: Instanced and expanded references agree without double transforms.

items.name: Memory budgets
acceptance: A refused job leaves the document and UI responsive.

items.name: On-demand textures and detail levels
acceptance: Missing tiles produce an explicit error or identified preview mode.

items.name: Responsive cancellation
acceptance: Cancellation releases owned resources and preserves the design.

items.name: Shader and preparation caches
acceptance: Cache keys include all relevant code and resource versions.

items.name: Multiple devices and distribution
acceptance: Merged output accounts for sample weights and failed work units.

items.name: Cross-executor regression
acceptance: CPU and GPU comparisons disclose unsupported features and numeric tolerances.

items.name: Appearance separate from engineering
acceptance: Changing a finish does not change engineering density or mass.

items.name: Face body and instance assignments
acceptance: An instance-only edit leaves its siblings unchanged.

items.name: Non-destructive render scene
items.benefit: Keep staging apart from CAD geometry
acceptance: Staging props and visual detail do not alter the design BOM.

items.name: Resource seed and version
acceptance: An offline reopen resolves the same declared dependencies.

items.name: Undo and lossless variants
acceptance: Applying a recipe is reversible as one logical action.

items.name: Portable scene and resource packages
acceptance: A package reports missing or restricted dependencies before export.

items.name: Shared UI CLI and MCP commands
acceptance: Programmatic commands never open interactive dialogs.

items.name: Sections transparency and exploded views
acceptance: Render state remains separate from authoritative assembly placement.

items.name: CAD geometry precision for rendering
items.benefit: Resolve small parts within large assemblies
acceptance: No cracks, self-shadow acne or lost small geometry at the test scales.

items.name: Multilayer interference coatings
acceptance: Reference angular and spectral responses are identified and reproducible.

items.name: Surface diffraction
acceptance: Diffraction is distinguished from thin-film interference and lens flare.

items.name: Retroreflection
acceptance: Source-camera separation changes brightness in the intended way.

items.name: Spectrally excited fluorescence
acceptance: The supported spectral model and energy accounting are explicit.

items.name: Phosphorescence with temporal state
acceptance: Decay follows scene time and survives a checkpoint.

items.name: Lenticular micro-optics
acceptance: View transitions follow the selected geometric or validated effective model.

items.name: Geometric curves and fibers
acceptance: Macro fibers remain geometric and distant fibers use a declared approximation.

items.name: Tiled high-resolution output
items.benefit: Admit 4K and larger masters within measured budgets
acceptance: A tiled result matches a full-frame reference without seams.

items.name: Celestial placement and visibility
items.benefit: Place Sun and Earth from a declared scene context
acceptance: Earth visibility and terrain occlusion are checked rather than assumed.

items.name: Radiometric and photometric unit boundaries
items.benefit: Keep LED and solar source units explicit
acceptance: Lumens, radiant watts and relative authoring gains are never conflated.
Basic source quantity and ownership checks are foundational; advanced spectral calibration is a separately gated extension.

items.name: Particulate surface phase response
items.benefit: Represent powder scattering beyond a flat diffuse approximation
acceptance: Multi-angle powder references distinguish authored from measured parameters.

items.name: Terrain detail hierarchy
items.benefit: Combine lunar horizon and sample-scale detail
acceptance: A close vial shot and wide rover view share a continuous terrain.

items.name: Persistent contact and track marks
items.benefit: Record sampling and wheel interaction visually
acceptance: Marks arise from recorded contact events and do not imply a soil solver.

items.name: Time-varying geometry at shutter samples
acceptance: All parts and shadows use the same simulation time.

items.name: Temporal image consistency
items.benefit: Avoid animated material and denoiser shimmer
acceptance: A static region stays stable through a moving-camera test.

items.name: Spectral LED authoring
items.benefit: Distinguish source spectra and phosphor behavior
acceptance: A declared RGB approximation does not claim spectral prediction.

items.name: Separate render and collision representations
items.benefit: Render detailed geometry while simulating bounded proxies
acceptance: Visual contact is checked against collision tolerances.

items.name: Time-indexed scene caches
acceptance: A frame identifies the physics and appearance state it consumed.

items.name: Content pack admission and streaming
acceptance: An oversized or incomplete pack fails before mutation.

items.name: Atomic preset composition
items.benefit: Apply quality studio and environment together
acceptance: An unresolved preset leaves the scene unchanged.

items.name: Visible fidelity and availability states
items.benefit: Expose what a recipe can actually deliver
acceptance: Concept, bound and validated states are distinguishable in UI and automation.

items.name: Baked simulation rendering
items.benefit: Render approved motion independently of live simulation
acceptance: Rendering never changes or re-solves the approved trajectory.

items.name: Reproducible batch manifests
acceptance: Every output can be traced to one immutable manifest.
